name: the Horoscope (the orient)
meaning: The place of the horoscope: "the twelfth part of the zodiac surrounding the horoscope, from 5° above the actual horizon up to the 25° that remains, which is rising in succession to the horizon;" For the body, "We must, then, in general observe the eastern horizon and the planets that are upon it or assume its rulership in the way already explained."
cite: III.10, Loeb p.273; III.11, Loeb p.307
source: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos, tr. F. E. Robbins (Loeb, 1940)
basis: meaning quoted; points: app weights following the order of I.24 and III.10 (Ptolemy gives no numbers)

name: the place following the horoscope
power: bears no aspect to the orient
meaning: Ptolemy gives this place no matter of its own. It bears no aspect to the horoscope, and planets that "bear no aspect at all to the orient" he calls "entirely powerless".
source: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos, tr. F. E. Robbins (Loeb, 1940)
basis: meaning quoted; points: app weights following the order of I.24 and III.10 (Ptolemy gives no numbers)

name: the place in sextile to the horoscope
meaning: Ptolemy gives this place no matter of its own; it is one of the places that decline from the angles. "For when the moon is setting or declining from the angles, she portends journeys abroad or changes of place."
cite: I.24, Loeb p.117; IV.8, Loeb p.421
source: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos, tr. F. E. Robbins (Loeb, 1940)
basis: meaning quoted; points: app weights following the order of I.24 and III.10 (Ptolemy gives no numbers)

name: the lower mid-heaven
meaning: Planets have less power "when they culminate beneath the earth" (I.24), and in the matter of length of life "for the whole region below the earth must, as is reasonable, be disregarded when a domination of such importance is concerned, except only those parts which in the ascendant itself are coming into the light." For the soul: "Evening stations and position at mid‑heaven beneath the earth, and furthermore, in the case of Mercury and Venus, by day evening settings and by night morning settings, produce souls noble and wise, but with mediocre memory, not painstaking nor fond of labour, but investigators of hidden things and seekers after the unknown, as for example magicians, adepts in the mysteries, meteorologists, makers of instruments and machines, conjurors, astrologers, philosophers, readers of omens, interpreters of dreams, and the like." With the 5th, it is among the places "diametrically opposite" the mid-heaven and the Good Daemon, looked to for children when those are empty.
cite: I.24, Loeb p.117; III.10, Loeb p.273; III.13, Loeb p.337; IV.6, Loeb p.409
source: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos, tr. F. E. Robbins (Loeb, 1940)
basis: meaning quoted; points: app weights following the order of I.24 and III.10 (Ptolemy gives no numbers)

name: the place in trine to the horoscope
meaning: Ptolemy gives this place no matter of its own, except for children: "we shall have to observe the planets that are in the mid‑heaven or in aspect with it or with its succedent, that is, the house of the Good Daemon, or, in default of such planets, those connected with the diametrically opposite places;" (the 5th is opposite the Good Daemon).
source: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos, tr. F. E. Robbins (Loeb, 1940)
basis: meaning quoted; points: app weights following the order of I.24 and III.10 (Ptolemy gives no numbers)

name: the place preceding the occident
power: bears no aspect to the orient
meaning: For bodily injuries and diseases "it is necessary to look to the two angles of the horizon, that is, the orient and the occident, and especially to the occident itself and the sign preceding it, which is disjunct from the oriental angle." That sign is this place.
source: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos, tr. F. E. Robbins (Loeb, 1940)
basis: meaning quoted; points: app weights following the order of I.24 and III.10 (Ptolemy gives no numbers)

name: the Occident
meaning: "the part opposite, the Occident." It is one of the two angles of the horizon looked to for diseases: "it is necessary to look to the two angles of the horizon, that is, the orient and the occident, and especially to the occident itself and the sign preceding it, which is disjunct from the oriental angle."
cite: III.10, Loeb p.273; III.12, Loeb p.317
source: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos, tr. F. E. Robbins (Loeb, 1940)
basis: meaning quoted; points: app weights following the order of I.24 and III.10 (Ptolemy gives no numbers)

name: the place disjunct from the ascendant
power: bears no aspect to the orient
meaning: "Of the part above the earth it is not fitting to consider either the sign that is disjunct from the ascendant, nor that which rose before it, called the House of the Evil Daemon, because it injures the emanation from the stars in it to the earth and is also declining," (the first of these signs is this place.)
source: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos, tr. F. E. Robbins (Loeb, 1940)
basis: meaning quoted; points: app weights following the order of I.24 and III.10 (Ptolemy gives no numbers)

name: the House of the God
power: declining from mid-heaven; fifth in authority
meaning: "the part in trine, called the House of the God;" It is the last of the places of authority. It declines from the mid-heaven: "For when the moon is setting or declining from the angles, she portends journeys abroad or changes of place."
cite: III.10, Loeb p.273; IV.8, Loeb p.421
source: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos, tr. F. E. Robbins (Loeb, 1940)
basis: meaning quoted; points: app weights following the order of I.24 and III.10 (Ptolemy gives no numbers)

name: the Mid-heaven
meaning: "the part in quartile, the mid‑heaven;" It is the first of the places of authority: "Among these there are to be preferred, with reference to power of domination, first those which are in the mid‑heaven, then those in the orient, then those in the sign succedent to the mid‑heaven, then those in the occident, then those in the sign rising before mid‑heaven;" For a person's work: "The lord of action is apprehended by two methods, from the sun and from the culminating sign." For children: "we shall have to observe the planets that are in the mid‑heaven or in aspect with it or with its succedent, that is, the house of the Good Daemon, or, in default of such planets, those connected with the diametrically opposite places;"
cite: III.10, Loeb p.273; IV.4, Loeb p.381; IV.6, Loeb p.409
source: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos, tr. F. E. Robbins (Loeb, 1940)
basis: meaning quoted; points: app weights following the order of I.24 and III.10 (Ptolemy gives no numbers)

name: the House of the Good Daemon
power: succedent to mid-heaven; third in authority
meaning: "the part sextile dexter to these thirty degrees, called the House of the Good Daemon;" Planets are "most powerful when they are in mid-heaven or approaching it", and this place rises toward the mid-heaven. It is looked to for children with the mid-heaven.
cite: III.10, Loeb p.273; I.24, Loeb p.117; IV.6, Loeb p.409
source: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos, tr. F. E. Robbins (Loeb, 1940)
basis: meaning quoted; points: app weights following the order of I.24 and III.10 (Ptolemy gives no numbers)

name: the House of the Evil Daemon
power: bears no aspect to the orient; injurious
meaning: "Of the part above the earth it is not fitting to consider either the sign that is disjunct from the ascendant, nor that which rose before it, called the House of the Evil Daemon, because it injures the emanation from the stars in it to the earth and is also declining," For slaves: "The special topic or account of slaves and the sympathy or antipathy of their masters to them is elucidated from the house of the Evil Daemon and from the natural suitability of the planets which regard this place."
cite: III.10, Loeb pp.273-275; IV.7, Loeb p.421
source: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos, tr. F. E. Robbins (Loeb, 1940)
